solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Talk about bosom, redhead's put together!

indicators.note: one piece goes round the others, as something placed about them encloses them

parts.note: to orate is to talk formally
bosom means chest
the head, or first letter, of the word red is R

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a red-haired person's assembled figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark is surface colour; 'put together' means arranged or organised, as an event is, and 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate an event is to organise and coordinate it, a synonym for putting it together.

clue.text: Put back record left in competition

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the word for a contest

parts.note: a race is a competition
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Restoring a record that was left in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to return it to where it was, to put it back.

clue.text: Past master

parts.note: read literally, an expert on the past, a scholar of bygone times, not an old hand at something

explanation.definitionFit: A scholar who specialises in study of earlier ages is a master of what is past.

clue.text: Floated on top of putrid bog

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: swam means floated

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something drifted on the surface of a stinking marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places SWAM above P, taken by 'top of' from putrid.
explanation.definitionFit: A swamp is wet marshy ground, a synonym for bog.

clue.text: Lock combination for altering without opening

indicators.note: combination signals letters mixed together into a new order
without opening means the first letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A lock combination is needed for changing something without opening it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without opening' drops the A from altering, and 'combination' rearranges LTERING. Lock is hair, not a door fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair.

clue.text: Transport bill carrying a team about

indicators.note: carrying means bearing inside, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: a tab is a bill
XI, eleven, is a team in cricket or football
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A bill for transport covering a team's journey around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link word here; the team is a cricket or football eleven, written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxicab is a hired car, a form of transport.

clue.text: Intrepid beating Mount Everest endlessly

indicators.note: beating means battering out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A bold climber conquering Everest without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the T from Everest, and 'beating' rearranges MOUNT with EVERES.
explanation.definitionFit: Venturesome means daring and willing to take risks, synonymous with intrepid.

clue.text: Small, voluptuous and dirty

parts.note: voluptuous means curvy in figure

explanation.surface: A description of someone short, shapely and filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurvy as an adjective means contemptible or low, as in a scurvy trick, morally dirty.

clue.text: Scraps lacking resistance in bars

indicators.note: lacking says one letter is missing from the longer word

parts.note: excerpts are scraps or extracts of text
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Fragments of something with no fight left in them, found in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes R from EXCERPTS. 'bars' is the verb, not drinking places.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to exclude or leave it out, which is what the verb meaning omit does.

clue.text: Attachment of woman welcoming former husband

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes them inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name
an ex is a former husband

explanation.surface: A woman's connection to her old spouse, whom she welcomes.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building attached to, or added onto, a main one, an extension.

clue.text: One Knight trying to trap Queen is unusual

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is knight in chess notation

indicators.note: to trap is to catch inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: testing means trying
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A chess knight attempting to capture the queen is a surprising move.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: the knight and queen are just letters, and 'is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something interesting holds attention by being out of the ordinary, loosely unusual.

clue.text: It's stir following bust for twister

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: something bust is broken or torn
a stir is a fuss, an ado

explanation.surface: A twister causes commotion after something breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link; 'bust' reads as a bosom or arrest but means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is an informal American word for a whirlwind storm of that kind.

clue.text: Dodgy pal with nice bird

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady friend in the company of a pleasant bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large waterbird with a throat pouch for catching fish.

clue.text: Frost reportedly wrote in this

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for frost is said out loud

parts.note: rime is a white frost

explanation.surface: The poet Robert Frost is said to have written in a particular form.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost looks like the poet, and he is in the surface, but it is also hoar frost, RIME, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Frost's poems mostly use matching line-end sounds, the verse form he wrote in.

clue.text: Album with 'Time' becoming timeless

indicators.note: becoming says the letters turn into something else, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A record including a song called Time becomes a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges ALBUM and TIME; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immutable never changes over time, so it is unchanging, ageless.

clue.text: Pleasure having bent for punishment

parts.note: read as enjoyment by someone with an inclination for being hurt, not a good time spoilt by penalty

explanation.definitionFit: The disorder is taking enjoyment from one's own pain or humiliation, a liking for suffering.

clue.text: Sailor hangs around for birds

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: slings means hangs, as from a hook
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor suspends something round birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlings are common speckled songbirds that gather in large flocks.

clue.text: Performer in part is tested

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the following words

explanation.surface: A performer's role is put through trials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning part is tested.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Girls with large behinds, capturing his heart

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: asses is slang for behinds

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Big-bottomed young women catching a man's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts I, the 'heart' of his, inside ASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassies is a Scottish and northern word for girls or young women.

clue.text: Moisten food's main ingredient retaining temperature

indicators.note: retaining means keeping something within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the base of a dish is its main ingredient

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice on keeping a dish wet and warm.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste meat is to moisten it with fat or juices while it roasts.

clue.text: Trail found in mountain stretch

indicators.note: found in says the piece lies within another

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a road is a trail or route

explanation.surface: A path discovered on a stretch of mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' is a verb here, not a length of land beside the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden is to widen or extend, which is to stretch out.

clue.text: Makes out with a wife to swing

parts.note: makes out means discerns, sees

explanation.surface: Someone kisses and cuddles with a married woman in order to swing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes out' looks like smooching, but it means sees; swing is a swaying motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to move back and forth or up and down, to swing to and fro.

clue.text: Awkwardly sit with same painter

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily, signalling the letters are arranged badly

explanation.surface: A painter's model sitting uncomfortably in the same pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leader of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: More gnarled tree?

definitions.meaning: a small tree with white flowers and black berries

explanation.definitionFit: Elder means older, more weathered by age, and is also a shrub-like tree of the honeysuckle family.

clue.text: Most fashionable bird embracing the French

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a coot is a black waterbird
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A trendy bird hugging French people.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool means fashionable in slang, so the superlative is the most fashionable.

clue.text: Perceived sixth sense that is dead

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the sixth sense

explanation.surface: Someone sensed by intuition that a person had died.
explanation.definitionFit: Espied means caught sight of or noticed, a synonym for perceived.

clue.text: Hostelry holds room back reserved

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry

indicators.note: back says the word for a room is read backwards

parts.note: a ward is a room in a hospital

explanation.surface: A hotel keeps a rear room reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the room into DRAW before 'holds' encloses it; reserved means shy, not booked.
explanation.definitionFit: An indrawn person is withdrawn or shy, a synonym for reserved in temperament.

clue.text: Weighing of certain hands in game

indicators.note: in says these pieces sit inside the other word

parts.note: game is wild animals as meat
sure means certain
hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: Weighing up particular cards held in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: Game here is venison and the like, not a pastime, and hands are workers rather than cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Weighing something is one way of taking its measure, a size or mass reading.
